name: Is countertop resurfacing or an overlay better than replacing the countertops?

mainEntity.name: Is countertop resurfacing or an overlay better than replacing the countertops?

acceptedAnswer.text: A countertop overlay may be less disruptive than full removal, but it is not suitable for every kitchen. The existing surface must be stable, adequately supported, and compatible with the overlay system; damaged cabinets, loose tile, poor alignment, or changes to sink and appliance openings can make full replacement more appropriate. Overlay thickness can also affect backsplash, edge, and appliance clearances. Compare the finished appearance, durability, repairability, and total installed scope rather than choosing solely for lower disruption. Elite Remodeling & Design can assess whether the existing conditions support a surface update or require a more complete remodeling approach.
acceptedAnswer.description: An overlay may reduce demolition, but it requires a stable, supported, compatible base and may limit sink, edge, backsplash, and appliance changes. Full replacement is usually more flexible when the old surface is damaged, uneven, or part of a layout update. Compare total scope and long-term fit, not just initial disruption.
